title: News the owner already saw on Today still counts as new in the bell and in the 11:00 summary
what: A news line on Today (someone joined, a payment came, a report came) leaves Today after one visit, but that 'seen' mark is kept only in this browser. The server never hears of it, so the bell's number still counts the line as new, the 11:00 summary push can still say there is a new update, and Today on another phone or computer shows it again as if it were fresh. Only tapping the line, or opening the bell, tells the server.
expected: Seeing a news line on Today marks it read for that person on the server, so the bell, the summary push and every other device agree.
how_often: every news alert seen on Today but not tapped
fix_line: When Today shows a news line, tell the server it was read, as the bell does

title: The owner can never see which members got an automatic reminder, or who could not
what: Automatic reminders (plan ends soon, plan ended, birthday wish, welcome and others) are on by default and each member's phone sets them itself. Nothing reports back. The Automatic reminders page shows only the switches and 'N of 11 on'. The owner cannot see that Asha was reminded her plan ends, or that she was not because she has no app, her number is not linked, she turned reminders off, or her phone blocks notices. Believing the reminder went, the owner does not chase her, and the renewal can be lost.
expected: The page shows, for the last days, how many members each reminder reached and how many it could not reach and why, with a list of those to message by hand.
how_often: every day, for every gym using automatic reminders
fix_line: Have the phone report each reminder it showed, and show reached and not-reached counts on the page

title: Messages offers 'Birthdays today' and 'Plans ending' groups with no word that the automatic wish and reminders already reach many of them
what: On Messages and offers the owner can pick 'Birthdays today', 'Plans ending within 7 days' or 'Plans ended in the last 30 days'. These groups take every member on the list. Members with the app who already get the automatic birthday wish or the plan-ending reminder that same day get a second message, and nothing on the page says so. Today's own birthday row and the AI ideas already leave out members the automatic wish reaches; Messages does not.
expected: These groups say how many already get the automatic message today and offer to leave them out, as Today does for birthdays.
how_often: each time the owner messages one of these groups
fix_line: Use the automatic-wish and reminder rules in these groups and show who already gets one

title: The 'Send members the app link' set-up step never ticks itself, though it says it will
what: Set up your gym says 'This ticks itself when your first member joins in the app.' The step counts as done only when a member on the list carries an app link, and the review of 16 Nov found nothing writes that link on real gyms (Crispy Curves: 2 app members, 0 linked). So the step stays open and the progress ring never reaches the end, however many members join in the app.
expected: The step ticks when the first member joins the gym in the app, by the same proof the server uses for app members.
fix_line: Tick the step from the gym's app members list, not from the unused link field

title: Set-up steps ticked on one computer are not ticked on the owner's phone
what: The set-up steps ticked by hand or by another screen (logo and colours, staff, timings, the check-in poster, link shared) are kept only in the browser where it happened. On the owner's phone or a second computer the same steps show as not done and the ring shows fewer steps finished.
expected: Set-up progress is kept with the gym on the server, so every device shows the same steps done.
how_often: every owner who uses two devices
fix_line: Save the ticked steps with the gym, or work each one out from the gym's real data

title: A MettleUp message read on one device still shows as new on every other device
what: Messages from MettleUp in the bell are marked seen only in the browser that opened the bell. The owner who read one on the phone sees it counted as new again on the desk computer, and each desk person sees it as new too. MettleUp cannot see which gyms have read a message.
expected: Seen is kept per person on the server, so a message read once stops counting everywhere for that person.
fix_line: Keep the seen mark for MettleUp messages on the server, per person
